one_line_contribution: It asks whether a success-only self-writing agent's failure to recover from a hidden ALFWorld rule change is worse than the displacement arithmetic that its own measured retrieval response function f(j) predicts, and pits that residual against a LoRA fed the identical self-collected stream, ending in a fitted per-substrate dose of fresh expert items needed to break the lock-in.
closest_prior_work: Closing the Feedback Loop (arXiv:2606.17591, verified this session via s2cli paper; S2 channel, 2026-06-16, 4 citations) is the real threat: it already reports that in non-stationary environments the same accumulated verbal experience either falls below the zero-shot baseline or improves sharply depending on whether a curation loop is present. That is the qualitative phenomenon this proposal opens with, already published, on a retention-forgetting framing. It does not kill the proposal — it governs the loop rather than measuring it, has no write-side starvation coupling, no parametric arm, no dose estimand — but it does mean the phenomenon is not the contribution; the decomposition (residual against the open-loop null) is. That shifts the entire weight of the paper onto the estimand, which is where the design is weakest. Second closest, also verified this session (hf): Honest Lying (arXiv:2605.29463, 2026-05-31), self-written reflections storing confident wrong task interpretations that persist across ALFWorld resets — same substrate, same self-confirmation, no rule change and no weights arm, so it is correctly positioned. Escaping the Self-Confirmation Trap / EDV (arXiv:2606.24428, verified, S2) is the repair-side analogue and is cited. I also verified 2607.13396 (Set-shifting Behavioral Test, hf), 2601.18642 (FadeMem, ICASSP, 11 cit), 2603.11653 (Simple Recipe Works, 12 cit) and 2609.00829 (HarnessEvolve, 2026-09-01) — all exist and are described as the proposal describes them.
strongest_objection: P1, the headline, is not identified. The open-loop Monte Carlo already contains the write-starvation feedback the abstract sells as the discovery: each simulated success appends one fresh item, and f(j) sets the success probability, so the simulated store starves itself exactly as the real one does. What is left in the residual R_s is therefore not 'the loop' — it is the ways the null is miscalibrated, and the proposal names the biggest one itself. f(j) is measured on the expert pool (E0), while the streams append self-collected items that P7 predicts are >=0.25*(s_fresh - s_stale) worse per item because they carry the stale detour. A null calibrated on better items than the arms actually write is guaranteed to over-predict recovery, so R_s < 0 is close to entailed and says only 'expert fresh items are better than self-collected fresh items', which is P7, not P1. The other residual sources the plan concedes (instance selection, age-similarity correlation, the interpolated f(1)) push the same direction. A skeptical AC will read P1 and P7 as one prediction reported twice, with the interesting-sounding half unearned. The revision successfully removed the definitional headline that sank opposite_sided_failure_under_shift, but replaced it with a model-dependent one whose null is calibrated off-stream.
what_would_fix_it: Calibrate the null on the same item population the arms write. Run E0's k=3 all-fresh and 2-stale+1-fresh cells twice, once with expert fresh items and once with self-collected post-shift successes from a pilot store, and define the primary residual against the self-calibrated f(j); the expert-calibrated version then becomes the decomposition (item quality vs residual coupling) rather than the headline. That makes P7 a prerequisite gate on P1 instead of a post-hoc mechanism probe, and it costs one extra 390-episode cell that the 1,000-episode reserve covers. Second, measure f(1) instead of pre-registering a linear interpolation — the whole winner-take-all claim in P5 lives on the shape between j=3 and j=0. Third, fix the units mismatch in P5: f is a function of top-3 composition and g of training-set fresh fraction, so 'winner-take-all vs graded' is being read off two curves on different axes; either evaluate the bank at k=9 to get a continuous fresh fraction, or evaluate g at the fraction that reproduces the bank's expected top-3 composition. Fourth, buy seeds: cut the recency-weighted bank (the proposal itself concedes its recovery is nearly entailed) and the 40 % bank placebo rung, and put those ~2,400 episodes into 5 seeds on the two headline arms, since every one of P2, P3 and P4 is a 'k of 3 seeds' binary.
missing_baseline: A paired no-shift control stream. The proposal cites Set-shifting Behavioral Test (2607.13396, verified) for pairing every shift with a no-shift control, then substitutes something weaker: each arm's own pre-shift window. That is a temporal control, not a control arm, and it confounds the rule change with everything else that changes over 400 episodes — store growth from 150 to ~350 items, top-3 retrieval quality as the store densifies, context length, adapter drift across eight chunks. Running the unbounded bank and the continual QLoRA for 400 further episodes under rule A (about 2,400 episodes) would tell a reviewer how much of the 'lock-in' curve is the shift and how much is a bank that simply gets worse as it grows; without it, P1's residual has a second uncontrolled source. Secondary omission: the escape-dose result (P6) has nothing to be dosed against. A zero-token read-side staleness heuristic — drop or downweight retrieved items whose procedure contradicts the agent's own most recent failure — is the cheap remedy a practitioner would try first, and the proposal cuts the failure-decayed bank on the grounds that read-side governance is 'already published' (2606.17591). Published elsewhere is not the same as measured here; an ED50 of 25-40 % expert items is only interesting if a free heuristic does not break the loop at 0 %.
preprint_collision:
No verified collision. The proposal's check is above the round's average — three concrete queries with returned IDs, seven IDs verified by s2cli paper, and four IDs (2606.00619, 2601.18226, 2606.05684, 2603.07392) explicitly dropped as unresolved rather than quietly retained — but it is thin in one specific way: this round's Q4-Q6 target the parametric side and the two added baselines, and the round-1 queries on the central mechanism (Q1-Q3) were dropped along with the IDs they depended on. So the mechanism itself was not re-searched this round, which is the search that matters most.
